messages.content: Airfare finally came down for North Texas. Can we lock it? I have Delta SLC–DFW Monday Sept. 9, 12:40 p.m.–4:15 p.m., and DFW–SLC Thursday Sept. 12 at 1:40 p.m. Southwest into Love is $88 less but lands 6:35 p.m. and would mean a different return airport. The Richardson and Denton cancellable room holds expire tonight, and the Fort Worth room has that tighter checkout.

Yes: I’d book the DFW plan. The Love Field savings isn’t enough for the later arrival, airport split, and reduced cushion before Richardson. Quick check before you pay: is the Richardson reception still doors at 6:15, program at 6:45, and are you carrying on?
Yes—doors at 6:15, program at 6:45. I’ll carry on. Thursday Denton breakfast should release me by 9:15.

Then book the Monday nonstop. Plan on rental pickup at DFW around 4:45; if the counter line runs long, go straight to Richardson before dinner. Return the car around noon or 12:15 Thursday for the 1:40 flight. Add the toll option only if it is pay-by-use, and skip prepaid fuel unless the rate is unusually low.
For hotels, do I still keep Grapevine/DFW North Tuesday, or switch that night to Fort Worth?

Keep Grapevine/DFW North for Tuesday. Fort Worth only helps one segment and the checkout window adds friction. Use Richardson/Plano Monday, Grapevine/DFW North Tuesday, Denton Wednesday. Cancel any Sunday hold and the Fort Worth backup once the three confirmations are clean.
What exactly counts as clean on the hotel confirmations?

Check free cancellation terms, parking fee, late-arrival note, breakfast or at least coffee timing, and room setup. For Denton, specifically ask whether food nearby will still be open if you arrive around 8:00–8:30 after Fort Worth.
Can you give me the cancellation dates for my calendar? Assume the hotels all say 6 p.m. local one day before.

Use Central Time and put reminders one hour earlier: Richardson Monday Sept. 9 stay: cancel by Sunday Sept. 8 at 6 p.m. CT. Grapevine Tuesday Sept. 10 stay: cancel by Monday Sept. 9 at 6 p.m. CT. Denton Wednesday Sept. 11 stay: cancel by Tuesday Sept. 10 at 6 p.m. CT. Tonight’s hold deadline is separate—book before it expires and save screenshots of the policies.
Seat requests and receipts—what should I not forget?

Choose a window seat if available on both legs; if seat maps are blocked, set a check-in reminder. Save the airfare receipt showing fare and taxes, rental confirmation with pickup and return times, final rental receipt, gas receipt, toll charges, and itemized hotel folios with taxes and parking separated.
American is $34 cheaper at about the same times. Still Delta?
If the Delta ticket is Main Cabin with seat selection and the timing is that close, I’d take Delta for $34. If it were Basic Economy or had no seat selection, I’d switch to American.
Delta Main Cabin, window seats open, no checked bag. I’m booking that.

Great. Final: Delta SLC–DFW Monday 12:40–4:15, DFW–SLC Thursday 1:40, window seats; DFW rental pickup about 4:45 Monday and return about noon Thursday; hotels Monday Richardson/Plano, Tuesday Grapevine/DFW North, Wednesday Denton. Add late-arrival notes, verify breakfast or coffee and parking, and release Love Field, Sunday, and Fort Worth backups after confirmations arrive.

messages.content: Next loop: late September Upper Midwest, Sunday Sept. 29 through Wednesday Oct. 2. I need to shape it before I put refundable holds down. Monday morning counselor breakfast in suburban Milwaukee, Monday evening fair in Madison, Tuesday visits in Janesville and Beloit, Wednesday afternoon transfer event near Rockford. Airports could be MKE or O’Hare. Main open questions are Sunday afternoon arrival versus first Monday flight, and whether Madison or Janesville is the safer Monday night stop.
I’d decide the arrival timing first because that affects the whole loop. What time does the Milwaukee breakfast start, what time does the Madison fair end, and how firm is the Rockford event window?
Breakfast check-in is 7:20, program at 8:00 in Brookfield. Madison fair is 6:00–8:00. Janesville is 9:15 Tuesday, Beloit at 1:30. Rockford is listed as early afternoon but not final.

Arrive Sunday. A first Monday flight leaves almost no margin for a 7:20 Brookfield check-in, especially with a rental car pickup and any weather or connection delay. Sunday afternoon or early evening arrival is the safe version of this trip.
Okay. For airport plan, compare MKE roundtrip, O’Hare roundtrip, and multi-city.

Three workable shapes: MKE roundtrip is easiest for Monday morning but makes you backtrack from Rockford on Wednesday. O’Hare roundtrip may have better nonstops and fares, but it adds a Sunday drive to Milwaukee before an early breakfast. Multi-city into MKE and out of O’Hare is the best route fit: shorter Sunday, no Wednesday backtrack, but you need to check the one-way rental fee.
MKE is one-stop from SLC. O’Hare has a nonstop. Is a connection into MKE worth it?

If the MKE itinerary has one comfortable connection and lands by early evening, yes. If the connection is under about 50 minutes, or it lands after 8:00 p.m., I’d take the O’Hare nonstop and drive to Brookfield Sunday. I would not use a Monday morning arrival for this schedule.
For Sunday night, airport hotel or Brookfield?

Brookfield or Wauwatosa, not downtown Milwaukee. You’ll be close to the breakfast, parking is more likely to be simple, and you can still get dinner nearby. Use an airport hotel only if the MKE flight arrives late enough that you’d rather not drive that night.
Monday after Madison is where I’m stuck. A Madison West hotel is available but pricey. Janesville is cheaper and puts me near Tuesday.

With an 8:00 p.m. fair end, Madison or Middleton is safer if you need dinner and rest right after the fair. Janesville saves money and helps Tuesday morning, but it creates a 45–55 minute drive after the event. I’d hold Madison as primary and Janesville as backup until the fair time is final.
I probably will need food after the Madison fair. Most of my afternoon is appointment blocks.

That leans Madison. Pick a west-side or Middleton hotel near actual restaurants, not just a campus-area room with inflated rates. Verify how late the nearby kitchens serve; a lobby market is fine for backup snacks, but I wouldn’t treat it as dinner after a fair.
If I stay Madison, Tuesday 9:15 Janesville is still okay?

Yes, if you stay Madison West or Middleton and breakfast starts around 6:00 or there is a grab-and-go option. Leave by about 7:45. That gives cushion for the drive, parking, and school check-in. Downtown Madison would be less appealing because it adds exit time and parking hassle.
Where should Tuesday night be: Beloit, Janesville, or Rockford?

Rockford. Since Wednesday is near Rockford and your return airport is likely O’Hare, it reduces morning risk and puts you in the right direction. Look around East State/I-90 or Riverside; those zones usually make parking and dinner easier than isolated highway exits.
Can you lay the route out simply?

Sunday: fly SLC to MKE, pick up rental car, sleep Brookfield/Wauwatosa. Monday: breakfast in Brookfield, drive to Madison, fair, sleep Madison West/Middleton if food access matters. Tuesday: drive to Janesville, then Beloit, then sleep Rockford. Wednesday: Rockford transfer event, drive to O’Hare, return the car, fly home.
What hotel details should I verify before I hold rooms?

For each hotel, verify breakfast start time, parking cost, cancellation deadline in local time, late-arrival policy, room bed setup, and whether they can provide an itemized folio. For Monday Madison, also check restaurant hours nearby. For Rockford, check that checkout will be quick before the transfer event.

I found Brookfield with free breakfast and parking, Madison West with breakfast but $15 parking, Janesville Hampton free both, and Rockford East State free both. The Madison option is about $70 more than Janesville all-in.

For now: hold Brookfield Sunday, Madison West or Middleton Monday, and Rockford Tuesday; also hold Janesville Monday only as a backup if it is fully cancellable. The $70 buys dinner access and avoids a late post-fair drive, so it is worth holding until the fair end time is final. Price flights as SLC–MKE Sunday afternoon with one comfortable connection, returning ORD–SLC Wednesday evening. Check the one-way rental fee and plan MKE pickup with ORD return.

messages.content: Upper Midwest update before I book: Madison fair now ends at 8:45 p.m. and the Rockford transfer event is confirmed Wednesday at 1:00. Madison hotels are tight because of campus weekend. I need the provisional route narrowed tonight.
That changes Monday night. Can you eat before the fair, or do you need a real dinner afterward? Also, what is the price gap between Madison and Janesville now?
Madison West is $239 plus $18 parking, cancellable only until tonight. Janesville is $144, free parking, breakfast starts at 6. I can eat at 4:30 before the fair and keep a snack in the car.

Then switch Monday night to Janesville, with a safety caveat. If the fair ends at 8:45, you can leave around 9:10 and arrive around 10:00–10:15, assuming normal weather and no dinner stop. That is late, but the price and Tuesday morning benefit make it reasonable.
Will that make Tuesday easier enough to justify the late drive?

Yes. Janesville turns the 9:15 visit into a short local morning instead of a pre-8:00 departure from Madison. Beloit is also straightforward from there. The trade-off is fatigue Monday night, so treat dinner as handled before the fair and don’t plan any extra stop afterward.
Airport pairing to price: still MKE in and O’Hare out?
Yes. Fly into MKE Sunday and out of O’Hare Wednesday. Don’t price a first Monday arrival. With Rockford confirmed at 1:00, use an ORD flight at 6:30 p.m. or later, ideally closer to 7:00.
Specific flight option: SLC–MKE Sunday via MSP, 78-minute connection, lands 5:40. ORD–SLC Wednesday nonstop at 7:10. O’Hare roundtrip is $60 cheaper but would land at O’Hare Sunday 4:55.

Take the MKE inbound if the fare difference is only $60. The 78-minute MSP connection is comfortable enough, and landing at MKE avoids a long Sunday drive before the 7:20 Brookfield check-in Monday. Keep the ORD 7:10 return; that is a good cushion after Rockford.
Hotel sequence, with the checks?

Sunday Brookfield/Wauwatosa: breakfast by 6:30 or grab-and-go, free parking, close to the 7:20 check-in. Monday Janesville: late-arrival note for about 10:15, breakfast at 6, free parking, and don’t rely on restaurant service. Tuesday Rockford East State/I-90: breakfast at 6 or 6:30, free parking, restaurants nearby Tuesday night, and quick checkout Wednesday.
Should I still hold anything in Madison?

Only until Janesville confirms late arrival and cancellation terms. Once Janesville is confirmed, release Madison; the campus-weekend rate plus parking is not worth it if you are willing to pre-eat and drive after the fair.
One-way rental MKE to ORD is $38 more. Return car at ORD or back to Milwaukee?

Return at ORD. The $38 fee is worth avoiding a backtrack from Rockford to Milwaukee. Put rental pickup at MKE around 6:15 Sunday and ORD return around 5:00 Wednesday for the 7:10 flight. Tonight: book refundable Brookfield, Janesville, and Rockford rooms; verify breakfast, parking, late arrival, cancellation times, and itemized folio availability; release Madison after Janesville is secured.
